definition: With normalized cluster indicators P, projected features are P^T X, propagation is P^T A_hat P, and the shared layer bias is multiplied by sqrt(cluster size). Query endpoints remain singletons. There is no second normalization or additional coarse self-loop insertion.
interventions: Recompute fine normalization and its projected operator separately for the full graph, each retained support, and each deleted support. The partition and projected original features stay fixed for each query.
controls: Authoritative full-graph predictions replayed from saved checkpoints and supports
Native GCN on the exact normalization-boundary region
Singleton-projection implementation that reuses one normalized operator across layers
Dynamic exact compaction rebuilt for each intervention
selection: Twenty validation queries per dataset/checkpoint, ten per class in the existing record order, without selection on approximation outcomes. Each has one full prediction plus retained/deleted predictions at three support budgets.
verification: All exact controls preserve binary decisions and pass the saved/full/local numerical tolerances. Source hashes, recorded absolute errors, binary comparisons, residual ranges, and alternating timing order were independently checked after execution.
timing_interpretation: Ratios below one mean the projected variant is slower than the exact singleton/operator-reuse control. All three projected partition variants have median ratios below one in both runs. The native-local implementation is also slower than that exact operator-reuse control in these measurements.
interpretation_correction: The original context incorrectly described native-local as faster. Its exact-operator/native-local time ratios are below one, meaning native-local is slower. This corrects prose only; no recorded measurement was changed.
timing_limits: Four alternating paired repetitions per query, one warmup per path, on a shared GPU. Each evaluation covers seven serial forwards, not batched proposal gradients or complete support search. Masking, normalization and projected-operator assembly are included. Offline partitions, region construction and prepared projected features are excluded and separately recorded; query membership restriction is not separately timed. Resident data/model/features are excluded from incremental allocation measurements. No general scalability conclusion follows.
theory_scope: Exact singleton recovery and an invariant-subspace example are tested. A Frobenius operator residual and feature projection residual are recorded for real queries; they are not decoder certificates. The Galerkin operator need not be a normalized graph Laplacian, so the manuscript comparison is stated for bounded symmetric operators.
decision: Do not use projected logits as authoritative explanation metrics, and do not claim a speed benefit for this implementation. Reduced node count alone does not establish faithful or faster inference. Retain this branch as a diagnostic and keep exact original/local evaluation as the reference.
next_work: Assess exact reuse of frozen feature transforms and layer-dependent computation before attributing any future acceleration to approximate coarsening. A batched or otherwise redesigned projected backend would require new accuracy and cost comparisons.
manuscript: Only operator assumptions and the bias/normalization derivation were clarified. Experimental values and tables remain unchanged.
